children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares rose on Wednesday as both Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix extended gains on sustained investor interest in the artificial intelligence trade. The won strengthened, while the benchmark bond yield fell.
** The benchmark KOSPI
was up 100.16 points, or 1.44%, at 7,054.68 as of 01:30 GMT.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 1.39%, while peer SK Hynix
gained 3.46%, after the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 1.3% in U.S. trading overnight.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed 0.29%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were up 0.26% and up 0.48%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 0.15%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
rose 0.03%.
** Of the total 909 traded issues, 405 shares advanced, while 448 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 174.3 billion won  ($130.2 million).

** South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and French President Emmanuel Macron discussed cooperation on security and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz during a summit in Paris on Tuesday, as the Middle East war intensified.
** The won was quoted at 1,339.1 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.28% higher than its previous close at 1,342.8.
** In offshore trading, the won
was quoted at 1,338.8 per dollar, up 0.1% on the day, while in non-deliverable forward trading its one-month contract (KRW1MNDFOR=) was quoted at 1,338.4.
** The KOSPI has risen 67.40% so far this year.
** The won has strengthened 7.5% against the dollar so far this year.
** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.01 point to 103.12.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 0.4 basis points to 3.899%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 1.1 basis points to 4.379%.
